imobitech.summary: Tech Lead at a Brazilian proptech. Led the Go rewrite of its real-estate CRM, built the Backoffice, docs and design system, and now write the backend of GO v2, its tax platform for brokers.

freelance.summary: My own practice, usually as the only engineer: an AI dermatology SaaS, a medical-shift marketplace, a drug-leaflet platform with an LLM layer, WhatsApp assistants with RAG, and data and KYC work.

nectar.summary: Took over SenseVox, the CRM's in-house VoIP product, after the telephony specialist left, and shipped it in place of Twilio at about 60% lower cost per service, with AI call transcription.

sevencred.summary: Built the Flutter app, the NestJS backend and the public-data pipelines of a credit fintech, and mentored a junior developer. The product closed before launch.

collectprime.summary: Kept a collectors' app alive on my own after the original team left: subscriptions through the app stores, the iOS app back on the App Store, and a NestJS rewrite.

ecto.summary: Moved Google Business Profile sync from a nightly batch to real-time events, cutting update time from up to a day to seconds. Led two developers and introduced code review.

vendorhub.summary: Built listing variations, an in-app image editor and manual orders across the Nuxt frontend, the NestJS API and shared schemas of a tool for Mercado Livre sellers.

ecto1.summary: Built the account, project and user-management core of Locasty, a Google Business Profile SaaS, plus bulk listing edits through the Google My Business API.

collectgram1.summary: My first job: wrote most of the internal Vue 2 back office and built marketplace pages in the Nuxt web app of a collectors' platform.

taglines.medical-shift-marketplace: A medical-shift marketplace: hospitals post shifts, doctors send offers, and contracts are signed in the app.

taglines.voip-platform: Cloud phone system inside a B2B CRM, with recorded calls, AI transcription and pay-as-you-go billing.

remote-harness.description: An open-source (MIT) app and self-hosted daemon for following and driving coding agents like Claude Code and Codex from an iPhone, iPad or Android phone. A Node daemon runs next to the agents in tmux, and a small Go relay forwards only encrypted traffic between the phone and the computer. In beta on TestFlight and the Google Play testing track.
remote-harness.role: Creator and lead developer: product spec, architecture, daemon, app, relay and store releases.
features: Approve or deny agent permission requests from the phone, even from the lock screen (iOS Live Activity, Android notification)
End-to-end encryption with the Noise protocol, per-device keys and single-use pairing codes; the relay only sees ciphertext
Daemon for macOS, Linux and Windows (WSL2), installed with one command
App, CLI and website in English, Portuguese and Spanish

go-v2-fiscal-backend.description: Imobitech's redesign of a six-year-old tax product for brokers. I wrote the Go modular monolith alone, contract-first, with a mock server so the web and Flutter teams could build in parallel. It connects to billing, e-invoicing and accounting providers. Go-live is planned for December 2026.
go-v2-fiscal-backend.role: Tech Lead and sole backend author.
features: NFS-e issuing with the IBS/CBS tax-reform payload
A queue for external-provider calls with backoff, call limits and an exception queue
Bookkeeping with spreadsheet import, protected against CSV formula injection
CI with a coverage gate, migration up/down checks and OpenAPI drift checks

dermatology-ai-platform.description: A multi-tenant platform for dermatology and aesthetics clinics, covering the consultation from recording to prescription. It has a web platform and a native app for professionals, a patient PWA, and an API that keeps a human acceptance step on every AI output. Consent and audit trail are built around Brazil's CFM 2.454/2026 rules on AI in medicine.
dermatology-ai-platform.role: Sole engineer: product design, architecture, all apps, infrastructure and store builds.
features: Live transcription and AI summary of the consultation
Prescription suggestions with citations (hybrid pgvector + full-text search)
Clinical record with a before/after photo timeline
Per-clinic branding, roles and PDF reports

medical-shift-marketplace.description: DoctorX connects doctors to on-call shifts at hospitals and clinics, replacing WhatsApp groups and referrals. A shift has a full lifecycle: offers, acceptance, chat, digital contract and mutual reviews. One Flutter codebase serves web, Android and iOS, backed by a NestJS API. In closed beta before launch.
medical-shift-marketplace.role: Backend, staff admin, docs and infrastructure; rewrote the legacy API and rebuilt most of the Flutter app.
features: Map-based shift search on PostGIS, seeded from Brazil's CNES health-facility registry
Medical license check against the CFM API during onboarding
Real-time chat with text, images and audio
Staff console with MFA, audit log, feature flags and payment kill switches

drug-leaflet-platform.description: Most leaflet sites just mirror ANVISA's PDFs. Bula Digital collects drugs, leaflets and master data every day, parses them into structured fields and uses an LLM to write patient-friendly versions. The backend is a NestJS modular monolith; the site is Astro SSR with React islands. Built for Ecto Digital; in pre-production.
drug-leaflet-platform.role: Sole developer: architecture, backend, frontend, LLM pipeline and infrastructure.
features: Daily ANVISA sync with leaflet version history (11,744 drugs and 6,780 leaflets structured)
Plain-language leaflets from a versioned prompt registry with golden-set evals
Faceted full-text search on Meilisearch
Admin with pipeline monitoring and LLM usage

voip-platform.description: Nectar CRM's in-house replacement for Twilio, built on Asterisk Realtime and NestJS. Extensions and numbers are created on the fly, calls are recorded and analysed by an LLM, and each service is billed from the account balance. It went live with a closed pilot of 4 clients at about 60% lower cost per service than Twilio.
voip-platform.role: Backend and VoIP owner; technical lead for transcription.
features: Asterisk over ARI, AMI and AGI, with call events queued so the API never blocks
Transcription with VAD + Whisper, plus a sales summary, sentiment and next steps
Multi-tenant accounts with per-tenant API keys and CASL permissions
Call-quality monitoring with Homer7 + Grafana

municipalities-chatbot.description: Citizens ask about services and public information on WhatsApp, and answers come from their municipality's own portal. A queue-driven pipeline collected and cleaned the portals of all 246 municipalities in Goiás and indexed them in Qdrant. It was demonstrated to city halls but discontinued before production.
municipalities-chatbot.role: Sole developer: backend, scraping pipeline, RAG agent, voice features and infrastructure.
features: Layered scraping: WordPress API, headless browser and PDF parsing (6,000+ pages and 20,000+ publications indexed)
RAG answers through a LangGraph state graph
Voice notes in, voice replies out
Multi-tenant model (organization → account → city hall)

miami-real-estate-assistant.description: A Miami luxury broker wanted a digital version of himself to answer leads on WhatsApp. A cheap routing model picks the right stage agent for each burst of messages, and the agents profile the lead, suggest at most three matching options and flag when the broker should step in. Their knowledge comes from his Dropbox archive, turned into a vector base and a structured catalog. Discontinued before launch.
miami-real-estate-assistant.role: Sole developer: architecture, backend, AI agents and data ingestion.
features: Five stage agents (welcome, profiling, search, scheduling, closing) behind a routing model
Voice notes in (Whisper), voice replies out (ElevenLabs)
Dropbox → Qdrant ingestion that built a catalog of 146 developments and 6,000+ units
CQRS modular monolith on MongoDB with RabbitMQ events and multi-tenancy

maarkn-dev.description: My personal site in English and Portuguese, built with Next.js 16 and React 19. It has an AI chat that answers from a knowledge base about my work, a résumé generator limited to that same base, and a private admin with an MCP server. It runs on my own server with Docker, Traefik and CI/CD.
maarkn-dev.role: Sole developer: design, frontend, backend, AI features and self-hosted infrastructure.
features: RAG assistant: OpenAI embeddings in PostgreSQL + pgvector, answers streamed over SSE, with rate limits
Résumé and cover-letter generator with structured output and anti-fabrication rules
MCP server with scoped API keys, per-tool permission checks and an audit log
Self-hosted: Docker + Traefik with Let's Encrypt, deployed by a GitHub Actions runner; WCAG 2.1 AA checked with axe-core

jobradar-ai.description: An open-source Python MVP that extracts job postings into a typed schema with an LLM, stores them in Qdrant and ranks them against a résumé. The idea behind it is that LLM output should be measured, so an evaluation harness runs from the CLI and in CI. The eval set is still small (3 synthetic cases), and it works on given URLs, not as a crawler.
jobradar-ai.role: Sole developer: pipeline design, LLM layer, ranking, API, dashboard, tests and CI.
features: LLM layer that switches between Anthropic and OpenAI with one setting, escalating cheap → strong models and logging cost per call
LangGraph ingestion (fetch → parse → extract → index) with per-step failure isolation and two-stage dedup
Résumé ranking with embeddings in Qdrant and explained match reasons
Field-level extraction evals in the CLI and CI; offline tests with mypy strict

cloudscraper-go.description: A Go library and CLI that fetch pages by sending the same TLS handshake as Chrome or Firefox, built on uTLS. It also has a rate-limited concurrent crawler, a session daemon and an MCP server for AI agents. It only passes TLS-fingerprint checks: no JavaScript challenges, no Turnstile, and no tagged release yet. Paused.
cloudscraper-go.role: Sole developer: library, CLI, crawler, daemon, MCP server, tests and CI.
features: Own http.RoundTripper on uTLS browser ClientHellos, speaking HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1; a fingerprint command checks JA3/JA4 against an external service
Concurrent crawler with a bounded worker pool, per-host rate limit and Prometheus metrics
Retries with backoff and jitter that honor Retry-After; HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5 proxies
About 40% of the code is offline tests; CI runs -race on two Go versions plus golangci-lint

museum-institutional-site.description: The society's old site only had posts. The new one, built from a Figma design, adds exhibitions, events, visit and ticket information, and the institution's first digital collection. Curators edit everything in Ghost and Directus, and pages still render if the CMS is unreachable. The MVP is ready; the launch is on the museum's side.
museum-institutional-site.role: Sole developer: frontend, CMS integration, infrastructure and deploy.
features: Digital collection with search and filters (denomination, author, class)
Ghost for posts and newsletter, Directus for structured content
Touchscreen kiosk page for a totem inside the museum
Docker Compose + Traefik with automatic TLS and an operator guide for staff

agritech-field-sales-platform.description: Sales reps use the app to plan and record visits to rural producers, including where there is no signal. I received the code as ZIP files, with no access to the store or domain accounts. I secured production with backups first, then documented, stabilised and migrated the platform from Oracle Cloud to AWS, validated on a production copy.
agritech-field-sales-platform.role: Sole engineer after the takeover: infrastructure, migration, documentation and mobile app.
features: Offline visit recording with sync
Offline-generated visit PDF report with photos
Automatic TLS with Traefik and Let's Encrypt, ending certificate outages
Sales-commission dashboard with PDF/Excel export, plus GitHub Actions CI/CD

carbon-credit-platform.description: A carbon-credit startup wanted an entry product for rural landowners: a first report on whether their land qualifies for carbon credits. A WhatsApp assistant sells the report and an Asaas link collects payment. Once paid, a pipeline crosses public CAR data with 15+ geospatial compliance layers and writes the report as a PDF, in about a minute and US$0.30 per report. The MVP met its grant milestone and was then discontinued.
carbon-credit-platform.role: Sole developer: technology choices, backend, AI report pipeline, checkout and infrastructure.
features: WhatsApp triage across about 10 intents, with human handoff
Asaas checkout with Pix, boleto and card
Report sections written by parallel LLM calls, exported to PDF
Web order page with CAR validation and a report editor

betting-audit-kyc.description: A regulated state lottery acquired an online-betting platform and planned to hand it to a new team. I audited six services (about 300k lines of untyped, untested JavaScript) across 16 areas, and the 15-item priority plan became the vendor's backlog. I also built the bettor onboarding: document capture, OCR and face match in the browser. The operation was put on hold before launch.
betting-audit-kyc.role: Code auditor and sole KYC developer.
features: 16-area code audit with 21 critical and medium findings and a prioritised action plan
In-browser OCR (Tesseract.js) and face match (face-api.js)
QR-code handoff from desktop to phone, synced over Socket.IO and Redis
Mobile-first PWA

fintech-loan-api.description: Groundwork for a fintech that wanted to score small-town businesses using public data. I built the Flutter app, the NestJS backend and the loaders and scrapers for government datasets. It stopped before production.
features: Batch loader of Receita Federal, PGFN, RAIS and PNAD data into MongoDB (14M+ rows moved off BigQuery)
SIGEF rural-property scraper written as the team's reference code
Flutter app with clean architecture, shipped to TestFlight for test users

collectprime-app.description: A Flutter app for collectors to catalog coins, banknotes and cards. After the original team left, I maintained the app, web and API on my own as a volunteer, shipped subscriptions through the app stores and brought the iOS app back. The product shut down in early 2026.
features: In-App Purchase with StoreKit handling and purchase restore
Apple and Google receipt validation on the API
Sign in with Apple linked to existing accounts
Parity tests between the legacy API and the NestJS rewrite

locasty.description: Ecto Digital's B2B SaaS for agencies and multi-store chains to manage Google Business Profile listings. I built the account and user core, then came back as Senior and moved data sync from a nightly batch to Google's real-time notifications.
locasty.role: Fullstack developer, then senior and main engineer.
features: Real-time review and Q&A sync through Pub/Sub
Bulk edits and scheduled posts across many locations
Insights reports with CSV export
Multi-user accounts with profile-based permissions

cloudscraper-js.description: A Node.js/TypeScript SDK on top of the Python cloudscraper library, published on npm. I forked an older wrapper by Eltik and rebuilt nearly all of it, with a long-lived Python daemon, reusable sessions and tools for AI agents. The Python library does the actual Cloudflare handling; this package manages it from Node. No longer maintained.
cloudscraper-js.role: Forked and rebuilt an existing TypeScript wrapper; maintained the npm package.
features: Long-lived Python daemon that keeps sessions warm, talking to Node over NDJSON with a buffered decoder
Exposed to AI agents as an MCP server, a LangChain tool and function-calling schemas, all on one set of handlers
Sticky proxy per session, with an explicit error when the proxy changes mid-session
Removed a sudo / curl | bash postinstall and added a non-root Docker image

imobitech.tagline: Leading engineering at a proptech: Go backends, a shared design system, and the rewrite of its tax product for brokers.
imobitech.context: Imobitech is a proptech in Goiânia that splits payments in real-estate deals and handles tax regularization for brokers. It runs several products (CRM, Backoffice, GO, payments) with a small team that works in Go.
responsibilities: Set the architecture standards (ADRs, Go guidelines) the team follows across products.
Mentor the four developers on AI-assisted, spec-driven development.
Build and run backend platforms: the CRM, the Backoffice control plane and the GO v2 tax backend.
Organize delivery: GitHub Projects boards, two-week sprints and a weekly status report for the board.
achievements: Rewrote the CRM backend from TypeScript to Go in under two months, with DDD, a Kafka transactional outbox and Connect-RPC, without breaking the production front end.
Turned tenant isolation into a check that runs on every build: a static analysis went from 79 findings to 0 with no exceptions, and 19 mutation tests prove each guard works.
Cut the inbox "awaiting reply" query from 2,419 ms to 18.8 ms on a synthetic dataset of 200k conversations.
Sole author of the GO v2 backend: 16 business contexts and a contract-first OpenAPI with 239 operations, plus a mock server so the web team could work ahead.
imobitech.outcome: Ongoing. The GO v2 backend is in alpha, with go-live planned for December 2026.

self-employed-freelance.tagline: My own consulting practice: AI products and fullstack platforms for startups and institutions, from architecture to deploy.
self-employed-freelance.context: Maarkn Dev Solutions is my company in Goiânia, and all the work is remote. Clients come directly or through partner companies: startups and institutions with a product idea or a stalled project. I own the technical side end to end: architecture, backend, web, mobile, AI, infrastructure and deploy.
responsibilities: Scope projects with founders and choose the architecture and stack.
Build backend, web, mobile and AI parts end to end, usually alone.
Set up infrastructure and deploys: Docker Compose and Traefik, with GitHub Actions on recent projects.
Run technical audits of existing platforms.
achievements: Built a multi-tenant dermatology SaaS with live consultation transcription and prescription suggestions backed by hybrid search (pgvector + full text).
Rewrote a medical-shift marketplace's API in NestJS + PostGIS, with map-based shift search, a staff console with MFA and B2B payments behind feature flags.
Built a daily ANVISA ingestion pipeline that structured 11,744 drugs and 6,780 leaflets, with a versioned, evaluated LLM layer.
Delivered RAG and agent systems with LangChain/LangGraph on Qdrant and pgvector, and WhatsApp assistants with voice in and voice out.
self-employed-freelance.outcome: Ongoing. Several projects reached MVP or pilot; some were discontinued by the clients before launch.

nectar-crm.tagline: Took over a stalled in-house VoIP product and shipped it to replace Twilio inside a B2B CRM.
nectar-crm.context: Nectar CRM is a B2B CRM SaaS. SenseVox was its own VoIP module (numbers, extensions, recorded calls, AI transcription, pay-as-you-go billing), built to replace the Twilio integration. When I joined, extensions could not be provisioned without restarting Asterisk, and the telephony specialist left in my second month.
responsibilities: Owned the SenseVox backend (NestJS, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis/Bull, RabbitMQ) end to end.
Ran the Asterisk/VoIP layer and its Docker infrastructure (Kamailio, NAT, TLS, fail2ban).
Designed pay-as-you-go billing per service, with balance top-ups through Asaas.
Was technical lead for the Python transcription service.
achievements: Moved Asterisk to Realtime (PJSIP on PostgreSQL), so extensions and numbers are provisioned without a restart; this had been blocking the project.
Replaced Twilio at about 60% lower cost per service, in production with a closed pilot of 4 clients.
Designed a 7-stage transcription pipeline: silence removal before Whisper, LLM analysis of sales calls, and model choice by token count to control cost.
Led a Python developer for about 4 months on the transcription service.
nectar-crm.outcome: Went live as a closed pilot during my contract; I left before the high-availability design for scaling past one Asterisk instance was built.

sevencred.tagline: Built the app, backend and public-data pipelines for a credit fintech that never reached production.
sevencred.context: Sevencred brokered FCO loans (a Center-West regional development fund) and wanted to become a fintech with its own regional credit score built from public data. The work was greenfield.
responsibilities: Built the Flutter app for borrowers and companies.
Built the NestJS backend: an Nx monorepo with a research microservice over Kafka and a CRM integration.
Loaded Brazilian public datasets (Receita Federal, PGFN, RAIS, PNAD) and set up Airflow.
Mentored the junior Python developer on shipping code behind APIs.
achievements: Shipped the Flutter app to TestFlight for test users, with Firebase and Google, Apple and Facebook sign-in.
Moved 14M+ rows of public data from BigQuery to MongoDB to cut query costs.
Built a lead pipeline on public data instead of buying a lead list of about R$50k.
Wrote a reference SIGEF scraper (Playwright, repository pattern) that became the team's code standard.
sevencred.outcome: The product never reached production: the owner stopped it after the government simplified FCO applications on its own platform.

collectprime.tagline: As a volunteer, kept a live collectors' app running alone: store subscriptions and the iOS app back online.
collectprime.context: CollectPrime is the collectors' platform where I had my first job, under its new name. With the original team gone, I helped the owner unpaid, a few hours a week, as the only engineer. Prime subscriptions were how the app made money.
responsibilities: Maintained the Flutter app, the Nuxt web app and the Express API.
Built and published app releases for iOS and Android.
Handled subscriptions on both app stores, with server-side receipt validation.
Planned and started the move of the API to NestJS/TypeScript.
achievements: Shipped Prime subscriptions through In-App Purchase on iOS and Android, with server-side receipt validation, and moved the existing card subscribers onto it.
Republished the iOS app on the App Store in about a week after it had lapsed.
Rebranded the app from Collectgram to CollectPrime and moved the web app to the new domain.
Ported about 70% of the API to NestJS, with a test suite that compares old and new API responses.
collectprime.outcome: The rewrite was never finished, and the company shut the product down in early 2026.

ecto-digital-senior.tagline: Came back as Senior to Locasty and moved Google Business Profile sync from a nightly batch to real-time events.
ecto-digital-senior.context: Locasty is Ecto Digital's SaaS for managing Google Business Profile listings, reviews and local SEO, sold to marketing agencies and multi-store chains. When I left it managed 400+ locations.
responsibilities: Fullstack development on the React front end and the Express/TypeScript/PostgreSQL backend.
Designed the event-driven sync with Google My Business notifications and Cloud Tasks.
Led and mentored two developers; introduced code review and gitflow.
Owned releases from v2.0 to v2.3.
achievements: Updates for reviews, Q&A and listings went from up to a day old to a few seconds, and server load spread across the day.
Moved scheduled posts and bulk edits across many locations onto Google Cloud Tasks queues.
Introduced code review and gitflow on a team of three.
Shipped every release from v2.0 to v2.3, and kept shipping after the team shrank to just me.
ecto-digital-senior.outcome: Real-time sync shipped and ran in production; I left for a fintech role.

vendorhub-sistemas.tagline: Built listing and order features for a SaaS that helps sellers run several Mercado Livre accounts.
vendorhub-sistemas.context: VendorHub is a small startup in Aparecida de Goiânia. Its product, Provendor, connects to the Mercado Livre API to manage listings, orders, questions and competitors. I joined a team of six developers on a live product.
responsibilities: Built listing and order features across the front end, the API and the shared schemas.
Mentored a junior developer and helped another with Vue.
Proposed code review as a team habit.
Fixed performance and caching problems in the live app.
achievements: Made the product-list query at least 80% faster; it used to take many seconds.
Shipped manual orders end to end, with stock deduction for products and variations.
Added an image editor inside the app (my idea), so sellers could edit product photos without leaving it.
Got code review adopted by the team.
vendorhub-sistemas.outcome: Features shipped to the live product; after four months I went back to Ecto Digital as Senior.

ecto-digital-fullstack.tagline: First fullstack role: built the account, project and user core of a Google Business Profile SaaS.
ecto-digital-fullstack.context: Locasty, Ecto Digital's SaaS, lets agencies and multi-store chains manage many Google Business Profile listings from one dashboard. I took over the position of a departing senior developer, who reviewed my code for the first two months.
responsibilities: Built features end to end on React and Express/TypeORM.
Integrated the Google My Business API for accounts and bulk listing edits.
Built sign-up, activation and password-reset flows with transactional email.
Fixed internationalization and rendering issues in the front end.
achievements: Let one customer account have many users, each with their own login and permissions, so activity logs show who did what.
Added bulk edits for logo, cover image and status across many listings through the Google My Business API.
Fixed an infinite loop when paginating a customer's Google My Business accounts.
Was hired back four months later as Senior.
ecto-digital-fullstack.outcome: Took over the codebase as the senior left; I moved to VendorHub and came back as Senior in October 2021.

collectgram-jr.tagline: My first job: built most of the internal back office and marketplace features of a collectors' platform.
collectgram-jr.context: Collectgram, a Goiânia startup later renamed CollectPrime, is a platform for collectors to catalog their collections, with coins and banknotes as the flagship. It had a marketplace close to launch and a Prime subscription. I was the only junior on a senior team.
responsibilities: Built the internal back office in Vue 2.
Built marketplace pages in the Nuxt web app.
Maintained the English and Portuguese translations.
Shipped through GitLab merge requests reviewed by the senior developers.
achievements: Wrote most of the back office: user onboarding with document review, orders, products, grading requests and a raffle MVP.
The owner used the back office every day to run the catalog and answer price requests.
Built product pages, public profiles, have/wish collections, sales and purchases, and subscription management in the marketplace.
collectgram-jr.outcome: After a year I left for a remote fullstack role.

whoami.role: Senior Fullstack Engineer · Tech Lead · AI/LLM systems
paragraphs: I take products from a rough brief to a working system: architecture, APIs, deploy and the messy data in between. I've built {products} products across proptech, healthtech, govtech, fintech and SaaS, usually as the only engineer or the technical lead.

Today I'm Tech Lead at Imobitech, where I led the Go rewrite of the CRM backend and write the backend of its tax platform. Most of my work is backend in Go and TypeScript plus LLM features inside products: RAG, WhatsApp agents, extraction pipelines with evaluation. I pick the simplest architecture that solves the problem and won't surprise whoever maintains it next.
I work with AI coding agents {{(Claude Code, Codex)}}: they write most of the code; I own the spec, the architecture, the review and what ships.
Open to senior backend, fullstack, Tech Lead and AI/LLM roles: remote {{(worldwide)}} or relocation to Canada, Ireland, Germany, Spain or the Netherlands.
